[[Category:Production]]
'''Production routing''' is the process of planning and organising the sequence of operations required during a particular [[production]] process.

It must take into account

* Tools and workstations
** Setup time
** Run time
** Maintenance time
* Labour
** Operation time
** Move time
* Process control
** Concurrency
** Inspection gates

<ref>{{#cite:Q3293}}</ref>

== Example ==

{{Hidden example}}
'''Production of 250 boxes of biscuits'''

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Routing for 250 biscuit boxes
! Op !! Work centre !! Setup (h) !! Run (h/unit) !! Run for 250 boxes (h) !! Queue + move (h) !! Op elapsed (h)
|-
| 10 || Weigh and mix || 0.40 || 0.006 || 1.50 || 3 || 4.90
|-
| 20 || Sheet and cut || 0.75 || 0.010 || 2.50 || 4 || 7.25
|-
| 30 || Bake || 1.00 || 0.020 || 5.00 || 6 || 12.00
|-
| 40 || Cool || 0 || 0.012 || 3.00 || 5 || 8.00
|-
| 50 || Decorate || 0.50 || 0.008 || 2.00 || 4 || 6.50
|-
| 60 || Pack || 0.30 || 0.005 || 1.25 || 3 || 4.55
|-
! Total !! !! 2.95 !! !! 15.25 !! 25 !! 43.20
|}

For operation $i$,

$$
t_{\text{run},i}^{(Q)}=Q t_{\text{run},i},
$$

and

$$
t_{\text{elapsed},i}=t_{\text{setup},i}+t_{\text{run},i}^{(Q)}+t_{\text{queue+move},i}.
$$

Total tallies:

$$
T_{\text{touch}}=\sum_i\left(t_{\text{setup},i}+t_{\text{run},i}^{(Q)}\right)=2.95+15.25=18.20\ \text{h},
$$

$$
T_{\text{elapsed}}=\sum_i t_{\text{elapsed},i}=43.20\ \text{h}.
$$

The difference is waiting time:

$$
T_{\text{wait}}=T_{\text{elapsed}}-T_{\text{touch}}=43.20-18.20=25.00\ \text{h}.
$$

Thus

$$
\frac{T_{\text{touch}}}{T_{\text{elapsed}}}
=42.1\%, \\
\frac{T_{\text{wait}}}{T_{\text{elapsed}}}
=57.9\%,
$$

so touch time is just over two fifths of the span (42.1%), while waiting time accounts for nearly three fifth. 

A scheduler that considers only touch time will promise an extremely unrealistic delivery date.
{{End hidden}}

== Contingency ==

In addition to an optimised '''standard routing''', it is often desirable to create alternative routings as backup, in case a particular machine/raw material is unavailable.

When subcontractors are hired, the planning concerning their work is known as '''phantom planning''', in which the general rule is to leave a generous '''time buffer''' for unexpected delays.
